chiefComplaints: Severe headache, persistent fever, and body aches
encounters.examinationNotes: Conscious, oriented, febrile to touch. Throat reveals mild erythematous congestion. Chest clear, no wheeze. CVS S1 S2 heard.
encounters.historyOfPresentIllness: Patient presents with high-grade intermittent fever for 3 days accompanied by throbbing frontal headache and generalized body aches.

admissions.admittingDiagnosis: Severe Acute Asthma Exacerbation with Hypoxia
admissions.dischargeSummary: Patient admitted via OPD referral in severe acute respiratory distress with wheezing and hypoxia. Commenced on IV hydrocortisone, nebulized salbutamol/ipratropium in ICU. Patient stabilized over 24 hours and was stepped down to General Medicine Ward. Respiratory rate normalized to 18/min, SpO2 98% on room air. Lungs clear on auscultation. Fit for discharge.
admissions.followUpInstructions: Tab Levocetirizine 5mg OD x 7 days. Budesonide inhaler 200mcg 2 puffs BD. Review in Respiratory OPD after 1 week.
